prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1, including identification of its active form and its glucose-dependent insulinotropic action, which made incretin-based treatment of diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: The round-1 exchange has narrowed the question to one thing: the third name on B027. Scientific merit, maturity and independent confirmation are not contested by anyone. The mechanism, from proglucagon processing and the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) peptide to human secretion and action, receptor biology and the therapeutic concept, has been confirmed for more than two decades, and randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease show the clinical consequence. As a neurologist I also value the central appetite-regulating action. I keep Drucker, Holst and Mojsov because the prize category rewards discovery, and the discoveries that made the target intelligible are the physiology (Holst, Drucker) and the identification and synthesis of the active peptide (Mojsov). I keep a single prize part: no member proposed a second one, and a second part would only compress the credit on the part that matters most.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and I have not removed it. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener, who is not on the credited list, cannot be settled from the supplied material, and I will not claim a documentary resolution that the file does not contain. Knudsen's design of long-acting acylated analogues is the step that made the physiology a medicine at scale, so a discovery-side trio can be read as honouring the hormone and not the drug. Also, B027 is mature but the therapeutic scope is still widening, and long-term safety outside metabolic disease is still being defined. These are real costs of my configuration, not rhetorical ones.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds Drucker, Holst and Knudsen: the analogue design that solved the half-life problem is itself a discovery, Mojsov's claim is the most contested, and the committee should decide whether the prize honours physiology or a physiology-to-medicine arc.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my configuration and I have reweighed it. I do not accept that Knudsen's work is merely industrial, since acylation and albumin binding is a mechanistic advance. But it is built on a target and a peptide that others identified, and the prize in this category is for discovery, so I answer the fork you and the chair describe as physiology-led, with the citation wording saying so. I also take your caution that Mojsov's claim is tied to the Habener question. Where we differ is the default: a contested priority is not a negative finding, and I would not drop her unless documentary evidence shows her contribution was not independent. If it does, I would move to Knudsen as third name, as you propose, instead of leaving a gap or naming only two.

responses.point: Perlmann prefers Mojsov to Knudsen because Knudsen's work is company drug development built on others' foundations, but offers a two-name Drucker and Holst prize as a cleaner fallback if the peptide record is unclear, and argues that contested priority is not weak science.
responses.response: I agree with you on the main point: Mojsov's contribution is necessary to everything downstream and her contested priority is a credit question, not a quality question. I part from your fallback. If the record showed she was not independent, a two-name prize would still leave out the drug-design step that carried the discovery to patients, so Knudsen is a better replacement than a gap, and a three-name prize is not forced by the cap but is not excluded by it either. On optogenetics you quote my rank correctly, with B015 second and B014 third. I accept that a tool must show changed understanding, not only changed practice, and for channelrhodopsin I think it does. I also agree that B014 is the cleaner credit, which is why I reorder my alternatives to B014 first.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius supports Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, wants the Mojsov priority review treated as the key step so she is not named on recollection alone, and says that if the discovery-side credit were too contested the cleaner fallback is a different candidate rather than a hurried reshuffle of names.
responses.response: I share the first point and I accept your discipline about recollection. My difficulty is the second: a different candidate would not be cleaner. B014 has a clean pair but a largely indirect medical consequence, and B041 and B015 carry larger credit holes than B027 does. A contested third name in a prize with otherwise settled merit is better handled by a pre-stated substitute than by abandoning the discovery with the strongest unanimous scientific case. You also note that long-term safety beyond metabolic disease is not yet defined. I regard that as an argument for a citation limited to diabetes and obesity, which I have done, not as an argument for waiting.

responses.point: Sandberg makes support for the trio conditional on a settled review of the priority question, says treating contested priority as a negative finding is wrong, and calls Knudsen the strongest argument against his own configuration.
responses.response: I agree with the condition and I want to be exact about what satisfies it. The supplied files do not contain the primary record, so I cannot say the review is settled. What I can say is that no member disputes Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active peptide as a contribution, only who had priority within the field. On that basis my support for her is conditional in the same way, and I name Knudsen as the substitute if the condition fails. I do not think it should be a surprise on the day of the vote, so I would have the committee state the substitute now, which is why I am recording it in this statement.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, relative to Habener, is independent and prior enough, which cannot be established from the supplied material and which decides between Mojsov and Knudsen as third name.
Whether the citation should honour the physiology and the active peptide or the physiology-to-medicine arc including long-acting analogues; I have taken the former.

Whether the long-term safety and expanding indications of incretin therapy outside metabolic disease should affect timing; I judge the diabetes and obesity evidence mature enough to support a citation limited to those.
Whether B014 or B015 would be the better second part if the committee reopened the single-part question; B015 cannot be given a defensible three-name credit from six claimants.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on B027, B014 or B015 is documented in my profile. I have roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann, who ranks B014 as an alternative, and I disclose this, though it does not concern the work of any credited candidate. My postdoctoral work with Paul Greengard involves no shortlisted candidate. I make no claim of any other tie, and as chair I do not treat support counts as a substitute for scientific judgment.
